statement: Trained practitioners of the Wim Hof method (cyclic hyperventilation + breath-holds + cold + meditation) could voluntarily activate the sympathetic nervous system (raising adrenaline) and attenuate the systemic inflammatory response to an injected endotoxin (lower TNF/IL-6, higher anti-inflammatory IL-10).
effect_size: Trained group: higher plasma epinephrine and IL-10, ~50% lower pro-inflammatory cytokines and fewer flu-like symptoms vs untrained controls after endotoxin.
population: Randomized controlled trial, 24 healthy men (12 trained vs 12 control), experimental endotoxemia

provenance.primary: Kox, van Eijk, Pickkers et al. — 'Voluntary activation of the sympathetic nervous system and attenuation of the innate immune response in humans', PNAS 2014

confidence_notes: A genuine RCT with a real immune OUTCOME, but: small n, healthy young men, acute endotoxemia model (not clinical disease). The intervention is a BUNDLE (breathing + cold + meditation) so the breathing component cannot be isolated. Adrenaline surge (mechanism) drives the anti-inflammatory effect.

statement: The acute anti-inflammatory effect of the Wim Hof breathing protocol is associated with a rise in plasma lactate/pyruvate during the practice, proposed as a metabolic mediator (alongside adrenaline) of cytokine suppression.
effect_size: Practice-induced lactate rise correlates with epinephrine and the dampened cytokine response.
population: Healthy adults practicing the method (mechanistic study)

provenance.primary: Zwaag, Naaktgeboren, Kox, Pickkers et al. — 'Involvement of Lactate and Pyruvate in the Anti-Inflammatory Effects Exerted by Voluntary Activation of the Sympathetic Nervous System', Metabolites 2020

confidence_notes: Mechanism. Helps explain the PNAS 2014 outcome; not itself a clinical outcome.

statement: An add-on Wim Hof-style program (breathing + cold + meditation) reduced inflammatory markers and disease activity in patients with axial spondyloarthritis in a controlled proof-of-concept trial.
effect_size: Lower ESR/CRP and disease-activity scores vs control over 8 weeks (small, open-label, proof-of-concept).
population: 24 patients with axial spondyloarthritis, controlled trial

provenance.primary: Buijze et al. — 'An add-on training program involving breathing exercises, cold exposure, and meditation attenuates inflammation and disease activity in axial spondyloarthritis', PLoS ONE 2019

confidence_notes: Disease OUTCOME but tiny, not blinded, bundled intervention. Hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory.

statement: A systematic review of the Wim Hof method found small, low-quality evidence: the most reproducible finding is acute anti-inflammatory/sympathetic effects, while broader physiological and psychological benefit claims are not yet supported by robust trials.
effect_size: Few studies, small samples, high risk of bias; consistent signal only for acute inflammation modulation.
population: Systematic review of WHM studies (healthy + clinical)

provenance.primary: Almahayni & Hammond — 'Does the Wim Hof Method have a beneficial impact on physiological and psychological outcomes...? A systematic review', PLoS ONE 2024

confidence_notes: The skeptical counterweight: highest-tier source in this domain and it counsels caution. Important guard against media over-claiming.

statement: Slow breathing (~6 breaths/min, near 0.1 Hz) increases heart-rate variability and shifts autonomic balance toward parasympathetic (vagal) dominance, and is associated with improved psychological measures (reduced anxiety/arousal).
effect_size: Increased HRV/RSA amplitude and baroreflex sensitivity at ~5-6 breaths/min; subjective relaxation.
population: Systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans

provenance.primary: Zaccaro et al. — 'How Breath-Control Can Change Your Life: A Systematic Review on Psycho-Physiological Correlates of Slow Breathing', Front Hum Neurosci 2018; Russo et al. — Breathe 2017

confidence_notes: Mechanism/physiological-correlate, well replicated for acute autonomic effects. Long-term clinical OUTCOMES are weaker/heterogeneous. Resonance frequency ~0.1 Hz aligns with baroreflex.

statement: The respiratory rhythm modulates cardiac vagal tone breath-by-breath (respiratory sinus arrhythmia): heart rate rises on inhalation and falls on exhalation, so prolonged exhalation increases parasympathetic activation — the proposed mechanism behind 'extended-exhale' and physiological-sigh practices.
effect_size: Longer/relatively greater exhalation increases HRV and vagal output vs equal or inhale-weighted ratios.

provenance.primary: Gerritsen & Band — 'Breath of Life: The Respiratory Vagal Stimulation Model of Contemplative Activity', Front Hum Neurosci 2018; Jerath et al. — Med Hypotheses 2006

confidence_notes: Mechanism. Grounds why exhale-emphasis breathing calms; does not by itself prove downstream health outcomes.

statement: Five minutes/day of cyclic sighing (a deliberate physiological-sigh, exhale-emphasized pattern) improved mood and reduced respiratory rate and physiological arousal more than equal-time mindfulness meditation or other breathwork in a randomized trial.
effect_size: Cyclic sighing produced the largest daily positive-affect improvement and lowered resting respiratory rate vs meditation/box-breathing/cyclic-hyperventilation.

provenance.primary: Balban, Huberman et al. — 'Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal', Cell Reports Medicine 2023

confidence_notes: Real RCT, real (self-reported) outcome. Short trial, healthy participants, subjective primary outcome; exhale-emphasis breathwork modestly beat meditation. Promising, not definitive.

statement: The Buteyko breathing technique (nasal breathing + reduced breathing volume to raise CO2 tolerance) improved asthma symptoms and reduced reliever-medication use in randomized trials, but did not change underlying lung function or airway hyper-responsiveness.
effect_size: Reduced symptoms and bronchodilator use vs control; no improvement in objective lung function (FEV1) or airway inflammation.
population: Randomized controlled trial, adults with asthma (Buteyko + pranayama vs control)

provenance.primary: Cooper et al. — 'Effect of two breathing exercises (Buteyko and pranayama) in asthma: a randomised controlled trial', Thorax 2003

confidence_notes: OUTCOME is symptom/medication (subjective + behavioral), NOT disease modification — the distinction matters. Buteyko's CO2/Bohr-effect rationale is contested; benefit may be from breathing-pattern normalization and reduced over-reliance on relievers.

statement: Diaphragmatic (slow, deep) breathing practice improved sustained attention and reduced negative affect and cortisol in healthy adults.
effect_size: Lower cortisol and negative affect, improved attention vs control after an 8-week diaphragmatic-breathing intervention.
population: 40 healthy adults, randomized intervention vs control

provenance.primary: Ma et al. — 'The Effect of Diaphragmatic Breathing on Attention, Negative Affect and Stress in Healthy Adults', Front Psychol 2017

confidence_notes: Small RCT, surrogate/psychological outcomes. Consistent with the slow-breathing autonomic mechanism.

statement: Nitric oxide (NO) is produced in the paranasal sinuses and is present in nasally-breathed air; nasal (vs mouth) breathing delivers this NO to the lungs, where it is a vasodilator proposed to improve ventilation-perfusion matching and oxygen uptake.
effect_size: Substantial nasal NO output; absent/low in mouth breathing; NO is a known pulmonary vasodilator.
population: Human respiratory physiology (ERS measurement standard + airway NO biology)

provenance.primary: Kharitonov et al. — 'Exhaled and nasal nitric oxide measurements: ERS Task Force recommendations', Eur Respir J 1997 (nasal NO); origin of nasal NO: Lundberg et al., Eur Respir J 1995

confidence_notes: MECHANISM. The existence and nasal origin of NO is solid; the leap to 'nasal breathing meaningfully boosts athletic O2 uptake/performance' is a weaker, popularized extrapolation not well demonstrated in performance OUTCOMES.

statement: The Bohr effect: elevated CO2 (lower blood pH) shifts the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve rightward, promoting O2 release to tissues. CO2-tolerance breathwork (e.g. Buteyko, breath-holds) is built on raising tolerance to CO2/blunting chemoreflex-driven air hunger.
effect_size: Classical physiology: higher pCO2 lowers Hb-O2 affinity (rightward shift), enhancing tissue oxygen unloading.

provenance.primary: Bohr, Hasselbalch & Krogh 1904 (classical Bohr-effect physiology); chronic over-breathing/CO2-tolerance framing reviewed in modern breathwork literature
provenance.surfaced_via: textbook/classical anchor (no single modern DOI; canonical physiology)

confidence_notes: Foundational MECHANISM (textbook, no single primary DOI pulled this pass). The Bohr effect is settled physiology; the claim that habitual 'over-breathing' impairs tissue oxygenation, and that CO2-tolerance training corrects it for health/performance, is a contested EXTRAPOLATION, not an established outcome.
